questions.q: What does a standard filter compare a field against?
options: A value you type in or choose
Another field on the same record
Whether a related record exists
The report type's primary object
questions.explain: A standard filter, like Stage equals Closed Won, compares a field to a value you supply. Comparing two fields or checking for related records needs a different tool.

questions.q: Which filter type would you use to find campaigns where Actual Cost is greater than Budgeted Cost?
options: A cross filter
The Show Me filter
A field-to-field filter
A bucket column
questions.explain: A field-to-field filter compares one field on a record to another field on that same record. You build it like a normal filter, but set the filter's Type to Field instead of Value.

questions.q: A cross filter is set to "Accounts without Contacts." What does it return?
options: Only accounts that have at least one contact
Only contacts that have no account
Accounts that have zero related contact records
All accounts, regardless of contacts
questions.explain: A cross filter with "without" finds primary records (accounts) that have no related records (contacts) of the chosen secondary object at all.

questions.q: Where in the Report Builder do you add or edit filters?
options: The Outline tab
The Fields pane search box
Setup > Report Types
The Filters tab, next to Outline
questions.explain: The Filters tab sits alongside the Outline tab. It lists active filters and has an "Add filter..." box for adding more.

questions.q: What does the badge next to the word "Filters" in the Report Builder tell you?
options: How many columns the report has
How many filters are currently active
How many records matched the report type
Whether the report has been saved
questions.explain: That small numbered badge shows the count of active filters, letting you see at a glance how narrowed-down a report already is before looking at its results.
